heading: INT. SALT MINE CURLING HALL, 400 FEET DOWN - NIGHT

units.text: INT. SALT MINE CURLING HALL, 400 FEET DOWN - NIGHT
Lamps hang from the cavern ceiling like drowned moons, and the ice beneath them has a faint pink cast from the mineral in the walls.
INGRID HALVORSEN, forties, shoulders wide as a door, crouches at the hog line with her broom across her knees, utterly still.
At the far house, TEODOR BRANICKI, thin and gray at the temples, wipes the same patch of ice for the third time with his sleeve.
BASH (BASHIR) QADIR, twenty-two, the youngest of the rink, hugs a thermos he has not opened.
His knee jumps against the bench.
Last stone. Weight's yours.
units.name: TEODOR

units.text: Ingrid does not answer.
She picks a hair from the pebble of the stone and flicks it away.
It's only a league game.
units.name: BASH

units.text: Then it won't hurt to do it right.
units.name: INGRID

units.text: She slides out of the hack.
The stone leaves her hand in a long, low whisper, and Bash is on his feet before he knows it, broom already sweeping, then not sweeping, then sweeping again.
The elevator cage groans somewhere above.
Boots on the iron stairs.
DESTINY OKAFOR-REYES, sixty, in a parka the color of traffic cones, steps onto the ice apron with a clipboard pressed to her chest.
She looks at the stone, then at Ingrid, then at the blank scoreboard.
Shift bell rang an hour ago. Nobody told you?
units.name: DESTINY

units.text: Teodor lowers his broom.
Ingrid keeps her eyes on the stone, which is still traveling, still curling toward the button.
Tell me when it stops.
units.name: INGRID
